1.d4 d5 2.c4 dxc4 3.Nf3 a6 4.e3 Bg4 5.Bx.strategy: Takes the gambit pawn back with a developing move: the bishop stands on the diagonal that presses on f7 and clears the way to castling. The bishop on g4 only eyes the knight on f3, which is defended twice, so White simply carries on developing.

Builds a solid pawn centre and opens the f8-bishop. Black has spent two moves on ...a6 and ...Bg4, so the plan is quiet development rather than a fight for the centre; the bishop is already outside the pawn chain, so ...e6 does not lock it in.
